items: 9 oz (250 g) hand-cut thick noodles (or any noodles you like)
1 tbsp white sugar (optional, but balances the heat)
1 tbsp chili crisp (+ 2 more tbsp extra for garnish)
More sliced green onion, for garnish

steps: Cook the noodles in salted boiling water, about 30 seconds less than the package says (they finish in the sauce). Save some pasta water, then drain and rinse under cold water so they don't stick.
In a cold pan (no heat yet), add the peanut butter, chili flakes, green onion, sesame seeds, garlic, sugar, 1 tbsp chili crisp, rice vinegar and dark soy sauce.
Heat the neutral oil until very hot, then carefully pour it over the ingredients in the pan and stir everything together.
Add the noodles and toss to coat. For extra silky noodles, turn the heat to medium-low, add 2–3 tbsp of the pasta water and mix well.
Turn off the heat and top with more green onion, extra chili crisp and lime wedges.

title: Smashed Beef Kebab With Cucumber Yogurt

items: 2 cups full-fat or low-fat Greek yogurt (about 16 ounces)
2 mini cucumbers (about ½ pound), grated on the large holes of a box grater
3 tablespoons finely chopped mint, plus mint leaves for serving
1 pound ground beef (preferably 80 percent lean) or ground lamb
1 small yellow onion, grated on the large holes of a box grater (see Tips)
¼ cup walnut halves or pieces
Warm pita or white rice, for serving

steps: Mix the yogurt, grated cucumber, chopped mint and garlic in a bowl, then refrigerate.
In another bowl, mix the beef, grated onion, turmeric, 1 tsp salt and plenty of pepper.
Heat a cast-iron or heavy skillet over medium-high until very hot. Break the meat into large rough chunks into the pan and leave it alone 6–8 minutes, until charred and crisp underneath.
Toss and break up any big pieces, add the walnuts and raisins, and cook 2–3 minutes more, stirring, until the meat is done and the walnuts are toasted.
Season the yogurt with the remaining 1 tsp salt and spread it on a platter. Top with the meat, a drizzle of pomegranate molasses and mint leaves. Serve with pita or rice.

items: 2 small broccoli heads (1 scant pound), cut into 1½–2 inch florets
Lemon zest, sesame seeds, fish sauce, chile crisp or chile oil, for serving (optional)
1 tsp fresh lime juice, plus more for serving

steps: Heat the air fryer to 375°F if yours needs preheating.
Toss the broccoli (including tiny stray bits, which get crunchy) with the olive oil, soy sauce and red-pepper flakes.
Move to the basket and scrape any leftover oil and soy sauce over the top. Fry at 375°F for 9 minutes, tossing halfway, until the florets are browned and crisp and the stems are tender.
Squeeze lemon over the top and add lemon zest, sesame seeds, fish sauce or chile crisp if you like.
Trim and halve the sprouts through the stems (quarter big ones). Heat the air fryer to 400°F if needed.
Put the sprouts in the basket, drizzle with 1 tbsp oil and the salt, and fry 15 minutes, shaking halfway.
Scatter the garlic over and fry 2–4 minutes more, until golden.
Meanwhile, simmer the balsamic in a small saucepan 2–3 minutes, until syrupy (watch closely so it doesn't burn). Off the heat, whisk in the remaining 2 tbsp oil, the lime juice and the soy sauce.
Drizzle the dressing over the sprouts and finish with more lime juice.
Heat the air fryer to 375°F if needed.
Toss the green beans with the vinegar, oil, red-pepper flakes, garlic (including any leftover garlic nubs) and salt, massaging the garlic onto the beans.
Move to the basket, scrape any dressing on top, and fry at 375°F for 8–10 minutes, tossing halfway, until charred in spots and tender.
Return to the bowl with any crisped garlic and sauce from the basket, season with salt, and serve hot or at room temperature.
Heat the air fryer to 400°F if needed.
Pat the salmon dry, brush all over with olive oil, and season with salt and pepper. If using, thinly slice half the lemon and toss the slices and tomatoes with 1 tbsp olive oil and salt.
Place the salmon skin-side down in the basket, top with the lemon slices and scatter the tomatoes around. Cook 5–7 minutes, flip, and cook 4–6 minutes more, until it flakes.
Squeeze the other lemon half over the top and serve.

items: 1 teaspoon thyme dry, 1 tbsp if using fresh
1 tablespoon oregano fresh, chopped, 1 tsp if using dry
4 cups chicken broth or vegetable broth, no sodium added
2 pounds chicken with skin and bones, use at least 1 chicken breast

steps: Set the Instant Pot to sauté and melt the butter. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook about 3 minutes, until the onion softens.
Season with the salt and pepper, then stir in the thyme, parsley, oregano and bouillon.
Add the broth, chicken and water. Don't add the noodles yet.
Seal the lid and cook on Soup (or Manual, high pressure) for 7 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for about 10 minutes, then open the lid.
Take out the chicken and shred it with two forks.
Add the egg noodles, switch back to sauté and cook uncovered about 6 minutes, until tender.
Turn off the pot, return the chicken, and adjust the seasoning.

items: 1 medium head broccoli cut into florets
Cilantro, green onion and sesame seeds (to serve)

steps: Stir the peanut butter, soy sauce, sriracha, rice vinegar, lime juice and ginger until smooth, then mix in the water a little at a time. Keep it fairly thick.
Heat the oven to 200°C/390°F.
Cut the tofu into about 1-inch cubes, toss with a few spoonfuls of the sauce, and spread on a lined baking sheet.
Toss the broccoli florets with the sesame oil, salt and pepper. Toss the chickpeas with the olive oil, chili powder, garlic granules, salt and pepper. Spread both on baking sheets.
Bake the tofu, broccoli and chickpeas for 15 minutes, turning halfway.
Simmer the quinoa with 375 ml (1½ cups) water and a pinch of salt, covered, for 15 minutes.
Thinly slice the zucchini and red cabbage.
Fill bowls with spinach, quinoa, tofu, broccoli, chickpeas, zucchini and cabbage. Drizzle with the remaining sauce and top with cilantro, green onion and sesame seeds.

items: 3/4 teaspoon coarse kosher salt (or 1/2 teaspoon table salt)

steps: Remove the skin, pat the salmon dry and cut it into 1–2 inch cubes.
Mix the brown sugar, both paprikas, chili powder, onion powder, garlic powder, cornstarch and salt.
Toss the salmon with the oil and the spice mix.
Spread in the air fryer without overlapping and cook at 400°F for 8 minutes (6–7 for medium), until golden and flaky.

items: 2 lb 3¼ oz Boneless Skinless Chicken Thighs
1¾ oz Reduced Sugar Sweet Chilli Sauce

steps: Spread a light layer of bang bang sauce on the chicken before cooking.
Oven bake or air fry 22–25 mins at 200C/400F until crispy and golden.
Spread an extra layer of sauce once cooked.

items: 700 g Boneless Chicken Thighs, cut small cubes
700 g Chicken Breast, cut into small cubes
400 g Fresh Tomatoes, de seeded chopped (makes it much less watery)
100 g Chilli Lime Hot Sauce (Brand: Cholula)

steps: Season chicken with marinade, mix well. Line a large sheet pan with parchment paper and lightly spray with cooking spray. Spread the chicken evenly and bake at 200C / 400F for 20-25 minutes until golden and juicy.
In a bowl, combine pico de gallo
In another bowl, mix taco sauce

Remove the chicken, leaving the juices in the tray. Stir paprika into the juices, dip the tortillas until coated, then fill with chicken and mozzarella. Fold tightly and bake at 180C / 370F for 15-20 minutes, flipping halfway until crispy.

items: 1 lb block extra firm tofu, pressed for 30 minutes then cut into 1” cubes or tear into pieces for even more crisp, (16 oz.)
½ tbsp light soy sauce, or liquid aminos
2 tsp cornstarch, up to 2 extra teaspoons for the best crisp
1 tsp sesame oil, or any oil

steps: In a bowl, add tofu and soy sauce and toss to coat. Add all of the other seasoning ingredients and toss to thoroughly combine.
Place in your air fryer in a single row, so each piece has a little space around it. Set the air fryer to 400°F and cook for 10 to 15 minutes, shaking the basket after 5 minutes.
Remove once cooked. Allow to cool for a few minutes, then serve.

items: 1 medium head broccoli cut into florets
1 400g can chickpeas drained and rinsed (air fry/roasted)
Cilantro, green onion and sesame seeds (to serve)

steps: Make the air fryer tofu (separate recipe).
Toss the broccoli with the sesame oil, salt and pepper. Air fry or roast the broccoli and chickpeas (about 15 minutes at 200°C/390°F, turning halfway).
Simmer the quinoa with 375 ml (1½ cups) water and a pinch of salt, covered, for 15 minutes.
Thinly slice the zucchini and red cabbage.
Fill bowls with spinach, quinoa, tofu, broccoli, chickpeas, zucchini and cabbage, and top with cilantro, green onion and sesame seeds.

items: ⅔ cup plain Greek yogurt or sour cream
10 ⅔ ounces burrata cheese, at room temperature

steps: Blend all the basil ranch ingredients until smooth and season with salt and pepper.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Lay the prosciutto flat on a lined baking sheet and bake 8–10 minutes, until crisp.
Cook the pasta in salted boiling water until al dente, adding the broccoli for the last 2 minutes. Drain.
Toss the hot pasta with the dressing, then add the corn and pesto and toss again.
Serve warm or cold, topped with the burrata and crumbled prosciutto just before serving.

title: High protein creamy tomato and basil beans

items: Small handful of torn fresh basil
250 g firm tofu - I used tomato flavoured but if you can’t find this, just use firm tofu and add a bit more tomato puree and salt

steps: Sauté the onions in plenty of olive oil and a pinch of salt for 8 mins. Add garlic and fry three mins more, then add tomato puree, the chopped fresh tomatoes and a big pinch of salt.

Bring to the boil, then bubble and simmer for 5-6 mins. Add the beans + their juices from the can (I pour a little out of the top first) and the basil, reserving a little for garnish. Bubble for a further 5 mins.

Scoop out 2 spoonfuls and blend with the firm tofu (I use a tomato flavoured one but if you can’t find this, add a little more tomato puree and salt) the nooch, and the miso. Add a splash or two of water to help it blend to a smooth consistency, season to taste.
Tip the tomatoey tofu cream into the beans, mix and gently heat.
Serve with yoghurt, olive oil, black pepper.

items: 200 g pasta (I used durum wheat semolina, Gemelli shape)
1 shallot or half a small white onion, finely diced.
200 g asparagus, woody stems discarded (use the snap method), stalks finely chopped, top parts left whole.
1 large courgette, sliced into thin half moons
480 g chickpeas, from a jar or can (I don’t bother draining if the can / jar is organic and BPA free)

steps: Cook down your onion or shallot on a low/medium heat for 5 minutes with a small pinch of sea salt. Add the finely chopped asparagus stems and cook down a further 6-7 mins.
Add the garlic, courgettes, asparagus spear tops and another pinch of sea salt to help that all caramelise. Add more olive oil if you need to.

Put the pasta onto boil for 1 min less than the packet suggests. Do not rinse when done, as this washes the starch off the pasta (which means the sauce does not cling as effectively!) Save one large mug of pasta water.
Add half the chickpeas to the pan, blend the other half with the miso paste, lemon juice and around 80ml of the salty pasta water.
Add the pasta and the creamy chickpea sauce to the pan, combine very well and add more pasta water if you think it needs it.
Top with EVOO, fresh black pepper, fresh parsley and optional roasted seeds (for an extra protein boost!)

items: 8 cups cauliflower florets (about 3 3/4 pounds, from 2 medium heads)
3 cups finely chopped stemmed kale leaves (about one 5-ounce bunch)

steps: Soak the cranberries in the boiling water for about 10 minutes, then drain.
Pulse the cauliflower in a food processor in batches of about 2 cups, roughly 10 seconds each, until couscous-sized.

Melt 2 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook the shallot and garlic about 1½ minutes. Spread the cauliflower in an even layer and leave it 5 minutes to brown, then stir and cook about 2 minutes more, until tender.
Add the cranberries, kale, half the almonds and the salt. Cover and cook about 2 minutes, until the kale is bright green. Stir in the sherry vinegar and move to a serving bowl.
In the same pan, cook the green onions, remaining 1 tbsp butter and remaining almonds for about 1 minute. Spoon over the couscous and serve warm.

items: 2 garlic cloves, grated on a rasp grater
One 8 oz block cream cheese, cut into pieces
1 1/2 cups bagged shredded Parmesan cheese (about 6 ounces; see Cook’s Note)
One 12 oz jar marinated quartered artichoke hearts, drained and halved lengthwise
One 8.5 oz jar oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, drained and chopped
5 oz baby kale or baby spinach (about 5 cups)
1/2 cup chopped walnuts, toasted, for garnish

steps: Cook the bow ties in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Drain and return to the pot.
Warm the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the cream and cream cheese and stir until melted.
Whisk in the Parmesan until smooth.
Fold in the artichokes, sun-dried tomatoes and kale, and season with salt and pepper.
Pour the sauce over the pasta and toss gently.
Serve topped with the toasted walnuts and chives.
Cube butternut squash
Sauté the onion garlic and a small piece of ginger (or use ginger powder) in olive oil in the instant pot
Add the pieces of squash and apple and sauté for another 5 minutes
Add salt and some ground cumin and coriander and brown some more for 5 minutes
Add some broth just to cover the squash and pressure cook on soup setting
After it naturally releases blend it

items: 1 tablespoon extra virgin olive oil, plus more for serving
2 to 3 cups store-bought chicken broth or Homemade Chicken Broth (page 216 in Magnolia Table Cookbook), as needed
6 basil leaves, stems removed, plus sliced basil for serving

steps: Warm the olive oil and garlic in a large pot over medium-low for about 4 minutes, until the garlic starts to brown.
Add the tomatoes and 2 cups broth, bring to a gentle boil over medium, then lower the heat.
Season with the salt and pepper, then slowly stir in the cream.
Add up to 1 more cup of broth for a thinner soup, then add the basil leaves.
Blend until smooth with an immersion blender (or carefully in batches in a blender).
Serve with a drizzle of olive oil and sliced basil.
Olive oil heat 🔥🔥🔥 in Dutch oven or pot
Add onions until translucent 🔥🔥🔥
Add garlic until fragrant 🔥🔥🔥
Add rice and stir for 5 minutes 🔥🔥🔥
Simultaneously, heat up broth in separate pot with saffron 🔥🔥🔥
Slowly keep adding broth to the rice so that there is a layer above the rice and keep stirring until al dente 🔥🔥
Before it gets al dente, you can add butter and/or parmigiano

items: 3 cloves garlic, minced and lightly sautéed

steps: Cut tomatoes in half parallel-wise
Remove core, seeds, and all liquid from inside of each half
Add a pinch of salt to each and put in pan
Add garlic, onions, pan grattato, salt, and olive oil and mix
Spoon mixture into each tomato, drizzle oil and a pinch of salt
Heat oven to 200C (375F) and cook for 1.25 hours

items: 15 oz medium butternut squash 2 cups cooked
2 tsp fresh thyme leaves removed from stem
1 lb rigatoni cooked to al dente
3 oz shredded white cheddar about 1/2 cup

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Halve and seed the squash and roast it on a lined sheet for 35–45 minutes, until fork-tender.
Scoop out the flesh and blend 2 cups of it with the ¼ cup milk, thyme and sage until very smooth.
Cook the rigatoni in heavily salted water until al dente. Save 2 cups of pasta water, then drain.
Mix the garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, salt, pepper, nutmeg and cayenne.
Melt the butter in a deep skillet over medium heat, add half the spice mix, then whisk in the flour. Slowly whisk in the ¾ cup milk until smooth.
Stir in the rest of the spices, the Dijon and the squash purée, and simmer on low.
Add the cheeses in two batches with splashes of pasta water, stirring until melted and smooth.
Fold in the pasta, adding pasta water as needed so the sauce coats everything. Serve warm.

items: ¼ cup thinly sliced red onion (optional)

steps: Toast the pecans in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 5 minutes, stirring, until fragrant.
Combine the greens, pecans, pears, grapes, cranberries, red onion and goat cheese in a large bowl.
Shake the maple syrup, Dijon, balsamic and olive oil in a lidded jar until combined, then season with salt and pepper.
Toss the salad with half the dressing, adding more to taste.

items: 2 (14.5-ounce) cans chickpeas (preferably not “no salt added”), drained and rinsed
2 ½ pounds honey nut or butternut squash, peeled, trimmed, seeded and cut into 1-inch cubes (6 cups)
1 ¾ teaspoons baharat, garam masala or another spice blend
1 ¼ teaspoons fine salt, plus more as needed
3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus more as needed
1 teaspoon cider vinegar or rice wine vinegar, plus more as needed
½ cup fresh cilantro leaves or dill sprigs, or a combination
1 to 2 tablespoons hot honey, plus more to taste
Plain whole-milk yogurt or sour cream, for serving (optional)

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Line one sheet pan with parchment and a second with a clean towel or paper towels. Gently rub the drained chickpeas dry on the towel-lined pan and leave them to dry while you prep.
On the parchment-lined pan, toss the squash with 1 tsp baharat, ½ tsp salt, the thyme, red-pepper flakes and 2 tbsp oil. Spread out and roast 20 minutes.

In a bowl, toss the chickpeas and red onion with the remaining ¾ tsp baharat, ¾ tsp salt and 1 tbsp oil. Add to the squash pan, stir, and roast 30 minutes more, tossing halfway, until the squash is golden and tender and the chickpeas are slightly crispy.
Sprinkle with the vinegar and herbs and toss. Drizzle with hot honey and toss again. Season to taste with more salt, hot honey and vinegar, and serve with dollops of yogurt.

items: 1 teaspoon apple cider vinegar or rice vinegar

steps: Cut all the vegetables into bite-sized pieces (keep the broccoli small).
Whisk the sauce ingredients together until smooth.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high and cook the chicken 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, until cooked through. Move it to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil and cook the onion for about 1 minute.
Add the snow peas, bell pepper, broccoli and carrots and cook 3–4 minutes, until crisp-tender.
Return the chicken, add the cashews, pour in the sauce and stir for under a minute until thickened. Serve right away.

title: Southwest Ground Beef and Sweet Potato Skillet

items: Kosher salt and fresh ground black pepper to taste
2 cups peeled and diced sweet potatoes
14.5 oz can fire roasted diced tomatoes

steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Brown the beef with the onion, breaking it up, then stir in 3 tsp chili powder, 1 tsp cumin, salt and pepper. Add the garlic for the last minute. Move to a plate and wipe out the pan.

Add the sweet potatoes, tomatoes, green chiles, water, the remaining 2 tsp chili powder and 1 tsp cumin, salt and pepper. Cover and simmer on lower heat about 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Stir the beef back in, sprinkle with the cheddar, cover about 1 minute to melt, and top with cilantro.

items: 6 bell peppers, tops and cores removed

steps: Preheat oven to 400°. In a small saucepan, prepare rice according to package instructions. In a large skillet over medium heat, heat oil. Cook onion until soft, about 5 minutes. Stir in tomato paste and garlic and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute more. Add ground beef and cook, breaking up meat with a wooden spoon, until no longer pink, 6 minutes. Drain fat.
Return beef mixture to skillet, then stir in cooked rice and diced tomatoes. Season with oregano, salt, and pepper. Let simmer until liquid has reduced slightly, about 5 minutes.
Place peppers cut side-up in a 9"-x-13" baking dish and drizzle with oil. Spoon beef mixture into each pepper and top with Monterey jack, then cover baking dish with foil.
Bake until peppers are tender, about 35 minutes. Uncover and bake until cheese is bubbly, 10 minutes more.
Garnish with parsley before serving.

items: Bread slice 1 (Sliced white bread without crust)

steps: Sauté veggies
Soak bread in milk chop into cubes. Fill milk almost to the top. Squeeze out milk from bread
Mush together everything with hands
Add salt and pepper
Make one big round ball
Sprinkle breadcrumbs
Baking pan
Oven 375F
Check after 30 mins
Should take 30-45 minutes
Shape dough into round flat shape
Oil and flour the pizza pan
Place dough onto pan
Spread spoonfuls of tomato sauce until whole surface area covered
Sprinkle cheese
Add affettato as topping
Add extra toppings like mozzarelline or cherry tomatoes
Add basil leaves
Preheat oven to 550F
Place pizza in oven and turn 90 degrees every 5 minutes until bottom is light brown

items: 1 can (12 oz) crushed or diced tomatoes

steps: Olive oil heat in pan 🔥🔥🔥
Add onions until translucent
Add garlic until fragrant
Add carrots and celery until brown put them to one side
Add beef until brown
Mix everything up and brown a little more 🔥🔥
Add salt and crushed tomatoes and stir together
Let cook for an hour and stir often 🔥-🔥🔥
When well amalgamated 🔥 for another 30-45 mins

items: 3 1/2 cups peeled and cubed butternut squash (from 1 small squash)
1 lb. Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved (roughly 12 ounces after trimming)
12 ounces (4 links) fully-cooked chicken sausage, sliced on a bias into 1/4-inch pieces (I suggest sweet Italian or apple chicken sausage)
Suggested for serving: cooked quinoa and arugula
1/4 tsp. each kosher salt and black pepper

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Spread the squash, Brussels sprouts, red onion and sausage on a large rimmed baking sheet.
Whisk the olive oil, maple syrup, rosemary, salt and pepper, pour over the pan and toss.
Roast 30 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and caramelized.
Meanwhile, mix the tahini, balsamic, garlic powder, salt and pepper, adding the water a tablespoon at a time until creamy.
Drizzle half the sauce over the pan and serve over quinoa and arugula with the rest.

items: ½ cup red bell pepper , chopped
½ cup salsa , I used Thick n’ Chunky Medium spice
15 ounce can black beans , rinsed and drained
½ teaspoon chili powder , use 1-2 tsp if you like more spice
2 cups chicken stock , or vegetable broth works too

steps: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium and soften the onion and bell pepper.
Add the beef and cook until browned. Drain the fat and season with salt and pepper.
Stir in the salsa, black beans, corn, tomatoes, green chiles, rice, taco seasoning and chili powder.
Add the stock and bring to a light boil.
Cover, turn the heat to low and cook about 15 minutes, until the rice is tender.
Stir, adjust the seasoning, top with the cheese and cover 5 minutes to melt. Serve with your favorite toppings.

items: Salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Whisk ¼ cup light mayo with ¼ cup Miracle Whip for the sauce (or ⅓ cup mayo, ½ tsp mustard and ½ tsp garlic powder).
Mix the ground chicken with the garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Spread a thin layer of chicken over one side of each tortilla and sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
Cook chicken-side down in a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high for 3–4 minutes, until golden and cooked through. Flip and crisp the tortilla 2–3 minutes.
Spread with sauce, top with lettuce, fold and serve.
Mush the avocados
Add the tomatoes, lemon juice, and (1/8) onion
Add 2 tsp pepper, 4 tsp salt
Wash beans
Sauté with oil and salt
Very quickly heat kashmiri chili, cumin, turmeric on skillet (less than half of chicken spice amount)
Mint, salt, pepper, basil grind into a paste
Mix paste and spices throughout yogurt
Cut chicken into 2-3 cm bite-size pieces
Heat (1/8) onions until crispy with garlic with some salt
Sauté the chicken until completely cooked
Add remaining coriander, kashmiri red chili, turmeric, cumin

items: ⅓ to ½ cup ice cold water
1 ½ cups shredded cheddar cheese divided

steps: Whisk the flour and salt in a large bowl.
Cut in the butter and shortening with a pastry cutter until the pieces are pea-sized.
Add the ice water a tablespoon at a time to one area of the dough, mixing with a fork and pushing the moistened part aside, just until the dough comes together (not sticky).
Gently fold the dough over a couple of times with your hands. Divide into two balls.
Roll one ball into a 12-inch circle on a lightly floured surface.
Roll it onto the rolling pin and unroll over a 9-inch pie pan. Trim to about ½-inch overhang and crimp the edges.
Heat the oven to 375°F.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Sprinkle the ham, 1 cup of the cheese and the green onions into the crust, pour the egg mixture over, and top with the remaining ½ cup cheese.
Bake 35–40 minutes, until the center is completely set. Cool 5–10 minutes before slicing.

title: Coconut Curry Salmon with Garlic Butter

items: 2-3 tablespoons spicy curry powder (homemade in notes)

steps: Heat the broiler.
Put the salmon on a baking sheet, coat with the olive oil, curry powder, salt and pepper, and drizzle with the honey. Broil 3–5 minutes, watching closely, until crisp on top.
In a large skillet over medium heat, melt 1 tbsp butter with the curry paste and ginger and cook 2–3 minutes, until fragrant. Stir in the broccoli, coconut milk, tamari and fish sauce.
Nestle the salmon into the sauce and simmer 3–5 minutes, until done to your liking.
Meanwhile, melt the remaining 5 tbsp butter with the garlic and a pinch of chili flakes until the butter browns and the garlic crisps.
Serve the salmon and sauce over rice, drizzled with the garlic butter.

title: Spicy Miso-Coconut Broth Noodles

items: 1 (1-inch) piece fresh ginger, chopped or grated
¼ cup tamari or low-sodium soy sauce
2 to 4 tablespoons chili paste, to taste (I like gochujang or Thai red curry paste)
1 pound cooked ramen noodles, Chinese-style egg noodles, or rice noodles
1 tablespoon toasted sesame oil, plus more for serving
Thinly sliced green onions, for serving
2 garlic cloves, finely chopped or grated

steps: Melt the ghee in a Dutch oven over medium-high. Add the mushrooms, garlic, shallots and ginger and season with red pepper flakes. Cook, stirring, about 2 minutes, until fragrant and starting to soften.
Pour in the broth, coconut milk and tamari, then whisk in the miso and chili paste until smooth. Simmer on low, stirring occasionally, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the noodles, spinach and sesame oil and cook 1–2 minutes, until the noodles are hot and the spinach wilts.

Meanwhile, make the sesame crunch: melt the ghee in a small skillet over medium-high. Add the panko, sesame seeds and garlic and cook, stirring often, 3–4 minutes, until lightly toasted. Off the heat, stir in the nori and season with salt.
Ladle the broth and noodles into bowls, spoon the sesame crunch on top, and finish with green onions and more sesame oil.

notes: Store leftover noodles and broth separately, since the noodles soak up the liquid as they sit.

steps: Prep veggies and cook sofrito in pan.
Add beef until well cooked
Add a spoonful of beef mixture onto empanada round, top with cheese.
Close empanada in half and use fork to seal the edges all the way around half circle. Do this on both sides
Heat olive oil on pan. Fry empanadas on both sides

items: Rana lasagna pasta ready to be baked

steps: Cook onion and garlic in oil over medium heat.
Add ground beef and cook 20–30 min over medium heat.
Add tomatoes and cook 1 hour, covered, on low.
Make a light besciamella in a separate pot (750 mL) and dilute with some milk.
Add some tomato sauce to the meat and cover again. Add some salt.
Layer order: A) besciamella, B) ragù, C) grated Parmesan, D) pasta sheets (Rana lasagne fresche all’uovo, bake straight in the pan; about 45 sheets).
Dollop a little of A and B in the pan before the first layer of pasta sheets, which should cover the bottom completely.
Repeat A to D for 6 to 7 layers of pasta, finishing with pasta.
Bake for 30 mins at 200C.
A freddo
Low per 2 ore

items: Greek yogurt, enough to coat chicken

steps: Salt the chicken and mix it in with the spices and yogurt
BBQ

title: Sweet potato rounds: herbed ricotta & walnuts

items: 1 large sweet potato sliced into ¼-inch rounds
¼ tsp sea salt to taste
1 cup raw walnuts roasted and chopped

steps: Mix the herbed ricotta ingredients and refrigerate.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Slice the sweet potato into rounds ¼–½ inch thick.
Rub the rounds with the avocado oil, salt and cinnamon, spread on a baking sheet and bake 20 minutes.
Flip and bake 17–20 minutes more, until cooked through with crisp edges. Roast the walnuts on a separate sheet for the last 8–10 minutes, then chop them.
Turn the broiler to high. Top each round with ricotta and broil about 2 minutes, until warm.
Sprinkle with the walnuts and cranberries and drizzle with honey.
Preheat oven to 350F.
In a bowl, mash the bananas.
Add in the other ingredients and stir together well. Use a spoon or spatula, not a hand mixer. This makes 12 cups.
Spray a 12-cup muffin tin with nonstick spray.
Add about 3 spoonfuls of the oatmeal mix to each cup, so they are about 3/4 full.
Add toppings.
Bake for 25–28 minutes, let cool for 10, then remove and enjoy!

items: 1 cup very smooth creamy natural peanut butter , or cashew butter
3 tablespoons pepitas, or crushed peanuts or cashews

steps: In a large bowl, stir together the peanut butter, honey, vanilla, and salt, until smooth.

Add the oats, chocolate chips and the pepitas (or nuts). The mixture might seem dry at first, but keep stirring and it'll come together. Stir to combine and press firmly into the pan. Use a second piece of parchment paper and the back of a measuring cup to help flatten the mixture. Chill for at least 1 hour, then slice into bars.
Store bars in the fridge.

items: Pinch of flaky sea salt (for topping)

steps: Line a muffin tin with 6 liners. In a bowl, mix oats, peanut butter, honey, vanilla, and cinnamon until fully combined. Press about 2 tablespoons of the oat mixture firmly into the bottom and slightly up the sides of each liner to form cups.
Mash raspberries with chia seeds and honey until broken down and jammy; let sit 5–10 minutes to thicken. Spoon the raspberry chia jam into the center of each cup. Sprinkle with flaky sea salt.
Freeze for 1–2 hours, until firm.
Let sit at room temperature for 2–3 minutes before eating

title: Key Lime Pound Cake

items: 1 cup/226 grams unsalted butter at room temperature, cut into pieces, plus more for greasing the pan
2 cups/240 grams all-purpose flour, more for flouring the pan
4 ounces/113 grams cream cheese at room temperature, cut into pieces
1 ½ cups/297 grams granulated white sugar
4 eggs at room temperature, lightly beaten
4 ounces/113 grams cream cheese at room temperature
¼ cup/57 grams unsalted butter at room temperature
¼ cup/60 milliliters Key lime juice

steps: Heat the oven to 325°F. Butter and flour a 9 x 5-inch loaf pan. Sift the flour and baking powder together.
Beat the butter and cream cheese on medium until blended. Gradually add the sugar and beat 5 minutes, until pale and fluffy. Add the eggs about a quarter at a time, mixing fully between additions.
Mix in the lime zest. Add the flour mixture alternately with the lime juice (juice in two additions), starting and ending with flour, mixing just until combined.
Pour into the pan, stopping ¾ inch from the top (don't use extra batter or it may overflow). Tap the pan firmly on the counter a few times.
Bake about 1 hour, until just set in the middle. Check at 30 minutes and tent with foil if the top is browning too fast. If it isn't set after an hour, keep baking and check every 5 minutes.
Cool in the pan 20 minutes, loosen the edges and turn out onto a plate with a raised rim.
Beat the cream cheese and butter until blended and a little fluffy, about 2 minutes. On low, gradually add the confectioners' sugar, then beat 20–30 seconds.
Mix in the lime juice, then microwave a minute or more until very warm and loose.
Poke holes all over the cake with a skewer. Pour half the glaze over, wait 10 minutes, pour on the rest and sprinkle with lime zest.

notes: Can be doubled for 2 loaves or a 10 x 4-inch tube pan (not a smaller Bundt pan). The glaze amount covers 2 loaves without doubling.

items: 1 stick or 4 ounces or 115g unsalted butter, at room temperature
⅓ cup or 75g light brown sugar
10 ounces or 295g strawberries, hulled and sliced ¼ inch thick (or halved blackberries, blueberries, pitted sweet cherries, sliced peaches, or figs)
3 tablespoons demerara sugar (you can use granulated sugar in a pinch)

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 9-inch cake pan and line the bottom with parchment.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt.
Beat the butter, both sugars and vanilla on medium-high about 5 minutes, until light and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time.
On low, add half the flour mixture, then half the buttermilk, then repeat, mixing just until combined.
Fold in half the strawberries, spread in the pan, scatter the rest on top and sprinkle with the demerara sugar.
Bake 45–50 minutes, until deep golden and springy in the center. Cool completely.

items: Grated zest of 1 lemon, lime, grapefruit or orange (optional)
12 to 16 ounces (340g–450g) raspberries or blackberries, fresh or frozen

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Spray a 9-inch round cake pan and line it with parchment.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt in a large bowl.

In another bowl, whisk the ricotta, 1 cup (220g) of the sugar, zest, eggs and vanilla until smooth. Fold into the dry ingredients, then fold in the melted butter and half the berries, crushing them a little.
Spread in the pan, scatter the remaining berries on top and sprinkle with the remaining ¼ cup (55g) sugar.
Bake 55–65 minutes, until golden and a toothpick comes out clean. Cool at least 20 minutes before unmolding.

items: 8 ounces/225g vanilla wafers or graham crackers (shy of 2 packages)
1 pound/450g/two 8-ounce packages cream cheese, room temperature
1 cup/240ml/8 oz sour cream, full fat greek yogurt or labne
2 tablespoons/12g finely grated citrus zest (lemon, lime, tangerine, etc)
Thinly sliced citrus, for serving, optional

steps: Heat the oven to 325°F. Crush the wafers or graham crackers into coarse crumbs.
Mix the crumbs with the brown sugar, melted butter and salt until it feels like damp sand.
Press firmly into the bottom and up the sides of a 9-inch pie plate or springform pan.
Bake 10–12 minutes, until the edges are lightly golden.
In a food processor, blend the cream cheese, sour cream and sugar until very smooth. Add the eggs, zest and salt and blend until lump-free.
Pour into the crust and bake until mostly set with a slight wobble in the center: 20–30 minutes in a pie plate, 25–35 in a springform.
Turn off the oven, crack the door and leave the cheesecake inside about 20 minutes. Cool 30 minutes at room temperature, then refrigerate about 2 hours.
Top with thin citrus slices before serving.

items: Nonstick baking spray or softened butter, for the pan
1/2 cup powdered sugar, plus more for garnish
5 tablespoons fresh lemon juice (from about 2 lemons)

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 9 x 13-inch glass baking dish.
Mix the flour, melted butter, powdered sugar and salt with a fork just until it comes together, then press evenly into the dish.
Bake about 20 minutes, until the edges are very lightly browned.
Meanwhile, whisk the granulated sugar, eggs and lemon juice until smooth.
Pour over the hot crust and bake 15 minutes. Loosely cover with foil and bake about 15 minutes more, until the center is set.
Dust with powdered sugar and cool completely in the pan before cutting into 15 bars.

items: ½ cup/120g heavy cream, plus more for brushing
2 cups/290g all-purpose flour, plus more for the work surface
⅓ cup/70g sugar, plus more for sprinkling
1 stick/4 ounces/115g cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
2½ cups/300g raspberries or blueberries, chopped strawberries, or halved blackberries

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Stir the cream and sour cream together. In a large bowl, whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Rub the cold butter into the dry ingredients until it forms flat flakes. Fold in the fruit, stir in the cream mixture, and knead a few times into a shaggy dough.
Pat into a 6 x 9-inch rectangle, 1½–2 inches thick. Cut into 4 pieces, then each diagonally, for 8 triangles. Space them on the sheet (chill 20–30 minutes for fluffier scones).
Brush with cream, sprinkle with sugar, and bake 25–30 minutes, until golden on top and bottom. Finish with flaky salt.

title: Lemon cake with cream cheese frosting

items: 1 tbsp grated lemon zest + 3 tbsp fresh lemon juice
1 tsp grated lemon zest plus 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Rub the sugar and lemon zest together with your fingers in a large bowl until the sugar feels moist, about 1 minute.
Whisk in the olive oil, then the eggs until well combined.
Add the milk, vanilla and salt and whisk about 2 minutes, until the sugar dissolves.
Whisk in the flour and baking powder just until combined, then give it 20 more turns around the bowl.
Lightly coat a 13 x 9-inch metal pan with cooking spray and pour in the batter.
Bake 30–35 minutes, until a skewer in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pan on a rack 10 minutes, then invert onto the rack and poke the cake all over 15–20 times with a skewer or fork.
Stir the honey and lemon juice until smooth and brush or drizzle over the warm cake. Cool completely, about 1 hour.
Beat the cream cheese, lemon zest and juice, and a pinch of salt on medium-high until smooth, about 30 seconds.
Add the butter and beat on high until pale and fluffy, about 1 minute, scraping the bowl as needed.
On low, gradually add the powdered sugar, then beat on high until fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Move the cake to a parchment-lined baking sheet and spread 1½ cups frosting over the top.
Refrigerate uncovered until the frosting firms, about 15 minutes.
Cut the cake in half crosswise and stack the halves. Frost the top and sides with the rest.
Refrigerate uncovered 30 minutes (or covered up to 3 days). Serve chilled.

items: 2 tsp grated lemon rind and juice

steps: Preheat the oven to 350F (about 180C).
In a large mixing bowl, beat the eggs and the sugar until the mixture turns pale yellow.
Add the lemon rind, the flour a bit at a time, the butter, and, finally, the baking powder.
Pour the batter into 9-inch baking pan that has been oiled and dusted with flour and powdered sugar
Sprinkle the surface of the cake with the nuts.
Bake the cake for about 50 minutes
Once the Mantovana has cooled, dust it with powdered sugar and serve

title: Apple Pie

items: 7 large Granny Smith apples (peeled, cored and sliced into ½ inch slices)
½ cup light brown sugar (loosely packed)
1 tablespoon lemon juice (plus the zest of half of a lemon)

steps: This pie has a top and bottom crust, so make two batches of the crust (double all crust ingredients).
Combine the flour and salt. Add the shortening and mix with a fork or pastry blender until very crumbly.
Sprinkle in the ice-cold water 1 tbsp at a time, stirring lightly after each, just until a little dough holds together when squeezed. You may not need it all.
Shape into two discs. Wrap and chill until ready to roll (up to 2 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen).
Peel, core and slice the apples into ½-inch slices.
Toss the apples with both sugars, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, lemon juice and zest.
Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the center. Let the chilled dough sit out 5–10 minutes.
Roll one disc into a 12-inch circle about ⅛ inch thick and fit it into a deep-dish pie plate.
Spoon in the apples, leaving the liquid behind.
Roll out the second disc, lay it over the filling, trim, then press and tuck the edges together.
Cut 4 slits in the top, set the pie on a baking sheet, brush with the beaten egg, and cover the edges with foil.
Bake 25 minutes at 400°F. Remove the foil, lower to 375°F and bake 30–35 minutes more, until golden and bubbling.
Cool at least 3 hours before slicing.

notes: For a richer crust, use butter-flavored shortening or replace half the shortening with butter.

title: Lemon Berry Glazed

items: 1 cup/240 milliliters good-quality olive oil, plus more for the pan
½ teaspoon kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal)
3 tablespoons finely grated lemon zest, plus ¼ cup lemon juice (from 3 to 4 lemons)
1 cup/200 grams granulated sugar, plus 2 to 3 teaspoons more for sprinkling
3 medium or large eggs, at room temperature
1 generous teaspoon vanilla paste or 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
½ cup/120 milliliters whole milk, at room temperature
1 heaping cup berries (blueberries, blackberries, raspberries or chopped strawberries), fresh or frozen

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Rub a 10-inch cast-iron skillet generously with olive oil (or oil, flour and line a 10-inch cake pan with a parchment round).
Combine the flour, baking powder and salt in a medium bowl.
In a large bowl, rub the lemon zest into 1 cup sugar with your fingers. Whisk in the eggs and olive oil, then the lemon juice and vanilla.

Stir the dry ingredients into the wet in three additions, alternating with the milk, without overmixing. Add the berries with the last addition of dry ingredients (if frozen, fold them in at the very end so they don't stain the batter).
Pour into the skillet, sprinkle with the remaining 2–3 tsp sugar, and bake 30–35 minutes, until lightly browned at the edges and springy in the middle.
Cool completely in the pan. Dust with powdered sugar, or whisk the 1 cup powdered sugar with 2 tbsp lemon juice and pour over the top.

notes: Keep covered at room temperature for up to 3 days, then refrigerate for up to 2 more.
